t: Founded in 681 by Asparuh's Bulgars among the Slavs south of the Danube, it was Byzantium's chief Balkan rival for three centuries.
Boris I's conversion in 864 and the schools of Preslav and Ohrid made it the birthplace of Slavonic letters and Cyrillic.
Under Simeon I (893–927) it dominated the Balkans; Basil II destroyed it after the Battle of Kleidion in 1014.
dyk: After killing the emperor Nikephoros I in 811, Khan Krum had the emperor's skull lined with silver and used it as a drinking cup, according to Byzantine sources.
ev: Byzantium makes peace with Asparuh's Bulgars, recognising the new state
Krum destroys the army of Nikephoros I, who is killed
Boris I accepts baptism from Byzantium
Boris I receives the disciples of Cyril and Methodius
Simeon I crushes a Byzantine army at the Battle of Achelous
Byzantium recognises Peter I as tsar and the Bulgarian patriarchate
Basil II destroys Samuel's army at the Battle of Kleidion
The Bulgarian nobles surrender to Basil II at Ohrid

f.capital: Pliska; Preslav from 893; later Prespa and Ohrid under Samuel
f.successor: Byzantine Empire (later the Second Bulgarian Empire, 1185)
